entry.title: Daily Briefing: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Executive Summary

It's launch week for Hermes Desktop, and the headline is Bot Screen: NousResearch's new feature lets you live-stream any agent's screen or session in real time, with human take-over built in. It arrived alongside Teknium's companion launch of interactive desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent. The announcement was the day's top post (~367k views), supported by official docs and a tonbistudio walkthrough, and community sentiment was emphatically positive — "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" replies frame it as a long-requested feature finally landing.

Beyond the launch, the ecosystem showed healthy grassroots momentum: rlaope announced oh-my-hermes (OMH) support for Jev skills, plugins, and model routing, and open-sourced jeval for evaluating and visualizing Jev results — positioning OMH as an all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent users. On the maintenance side, Teknium triaged publicly and actively: dismissed a reported cache issue pending a reproducible bug report, confirmed a quick fix for a user-reported problem, and corrected attribution of a discussed feature to Nous rather than Anthropic — a visible maintainer presence that reinforced trust during launch week.

On the tips front, NousResearch reminded users that Hermes can run over iMessage with any model of their choosing — another example of ongoing efforts to lower friction and highlight the agent's model-agnostic design. Rounding out the day, community chatter weighed in on Claude Opus 5.5 (released September 22), with rlaope calling the model "crazy" (impressive) while staying lukewarm on Claude Code — timely competitor context running alongside the Hermes launch coverage.
